functional_semantics.triton: C = A @ B into a fresh (M, N) tensor of a.dtype, fp32 accumulation, TF32 dot for fp32, half dtypes cast at the end by out.copy_(c) (impl_triton.py 124, 162, 257-262, 284-285).
functional_semantics.cutile: C = A @ B into a fresh (M, N) tensor of a.dtype, fp32 accumulation, operands cast to tfloat32 for fp32, half dtypes cast at the end by out.copy_(c) (impl_cutile.py 73, 89-92, 130, 205-212, 244-245).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise torch.matmul(a, b) under allow_tf32 = True (impl_torch.py 3, 7); verify atol 1.0 / rtol 1e-2 (config.yaml 1-3).

stages.triton: zero-fill of fp32 c (258-262); first_wave grid (NUM_SMS,) with atomic-add fixup (88-135, 197); full_tiles grid (blocking_tiles,) with TMA store, launched only when > 0 (138-165, 278-282); out.copy_(c) for half dtypes (284-285).
stages.cutile: zero-fill of fp32 c (208-212); first_wave grid (NUM_SMS,1,1) with ct.atomic_add fixup (47-103, 226); full_tiles grid (blocking_tiles,1,1) with ct.store, launched only when > 0 (106-143, 230-235); out.copy_(c) for half dtypes (244-245).
stages.note: Identical four-stage hybrid Stream-K pipeline with the same partition rule (streamk_tiles = total mod NUM_SMS, + NUM_SMS when total - streamk_tiles > NUM_SMS: Triton 96-100 / 172-177, cuTile 58-64 / 39-44) and the same even iteration split with leading programs taking the remainder (Triton 101-107, cuTile 65-71).

dependencies.triton: first_wave and full_tiles both require the zeroed c and write disjoint tiles (tile_id < streamk_tiles vs >= streamk_tiles, 110 / 150); copy_ after both (284).
dependencies.cutile: Same disjoint tile ownership (79 vs 124); copy_ after both (244).
dependencies.note: Same dependency graph: zero-fill -> {Stream-K wave, data-parallel tiles} -> final cast.

reduction_scan_sort.triton: K reduced in slabs via tl.dot into an fp32 accumulator; Stream-K segments combined by fp32 tl.atomic_add into zeroed c (118-133); full tiles sequential over tl.range(cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)) (158-162); grouped swizzle (74-85).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: K reduced in chunks via ct.mma into an fp32 accumulator; segments combined by fp32 ct.atomic_add into zeroed c (82-101); full tiles sequential over range(num_tiles_k) (132-140); grouped swizzle (28-36).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same per-tile fp32 slab reduction, same atomic combination (non-deterministic order for split tiles), same grouped-M swizzle arithmetic on both sides.

precision.triton: ACC_TYPE=tl.float32 (189, 202); tl.dot(..., input_precision='tf32') on both kernels (124, 162); c always fp32; single downcast via out.copy_ (285).
precision.cutile: ct.full(..., ct.float32) accumulators (82, 132); operands astype(ct.tfloat32) when A is fp32, else native (73, 89-91, 130, 137-139); c always fp32; single downcast via out.copy_ (245).
precision.note: fp32 accumulation, TF32 operand rounding for fp32 inputs, one final rounding for half dtypes on both sides. The Triton tf32 flag is presumed a no-op for half operands (standard semantics, not verified here).

preprocessing.triton: bt = _b_transposed(b): b.t().contiguous() cached per b tensor identity in a WeakTensorKeyDictionary (63-71, 264), so the (N, K) transpose copy runs once per input tensor and is untimed in steady state; host TensorDescriptors for a, bt (and c) rebuilt per launch (182-184, 195-196); NUM_SMS query (253); out allocation and zero-fill (257-262).
preprocessing.cutile: No repack: B consumed as the given (K, N) row-major tensor with (TK, TN) loads (90-91, 138-139); NUM_SMS query (203); out allocation and zero-fill (205-212); autotune-path scratch (219).
preprocessing.note: Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): B is delivered row-major; consuming it as given (cuTile side) or through a transposed copy rebuilt by device work inside every run() is a mapping choice, so the layout divergence is mapping-only. A B repack, if used, is per call and timed; no cross-call derived cache is permitted, so the manual Triton kernel's identity-cached, untimed B^T (impl_triton.py 63-71, 264) does not conform to the decided rule and its column is recorded as not comparable (human_reference_comparable = false); this is a reference-measurement caveat, not a contract ambiguity. The Stream-K decomposition / global accumulation structure is preserved on both sides.

intermediate_storage.triton: c: fp32 (M, N) accumulation buffer (out itself for fp32, torch.zeros for half dtypes, 258-262) plus the module-level cross-call cache holding an (N, K) copy of every b seen (63-71).
intermediate_storage.cutile: c: fp32 (M, N) accumulation buffer (out itself for fp32, torch.zeros for half dtypes, 208-212); no cross-call storage.
intermediate_storage.note: Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): the per-call fp32 accumulation buffer is the canonical (aligned) intermediate; a per-call transposed operand copy is a permitted, counted mapping-level intermediate; a copy that outlives the call via a cross-call cache is forbidden. The Triton side's persistent (N, K) copy is the non-conforming case covered by human_reference_comparable = false.

mutation.triton: a, b read-only; out fresh and zeroed/overwritten each call (257-262, 285); the B^T cache keys on identity so in-place edits of b between calls would be ignored (63-71).
mutation.cutile: a, b read-only; out fresh and zeroed/overwritten each call (205-212, 245).
mutation.note: No input mutation; idempotent outputs on both sides. The stale-cache hazard is a consequence of the preprocessing divergence, not a mutation.

hardware_dispatch.triton: detect_arch() selects a smaller K tile for the non-autotuned path on cdna3 and on hopper+fp32 (43-56, legality only; members of the unchanged search space); TMA TensorDescriptor loads (182-183, 195-196); NUM_SMS from the device (168-169).
hardware_dispatch.cutile: NUM_SMS from the device as a ConstInt (192-193, 51, 110); dtype branch to tfloat32 inside the kernels (73, 130); no architecture branches.
hardware_dispatch.note: All branches are legality/mapping (tile fallback, TMA vs tile loads) or dtype dispatch; the SM-count-dependent partition changes which program computes what, not the result. No algorithmic divergence.

fq_boundary.bytes_expr: (m * k + k * n + m * n) * dtype_size
fq_boundary.note: flops_expr = 2mnk matches the GEMM. bytes_expr (config.yaml 21) counts one read of A and B and one write of C in the input dtype. Decided 2026-10-06 (owner, FINAL_FREEZE_AND_START_B200.md §3): Q for scoring remains this explicitly declared lower-bound / compulsory-I/O model; the scratch traffic, the atomic read-modify-write of the Stream-K tiles, the per-call zero-fill of the fp32 accumulation buffer (m*n*4 bytes), the fp16/bf16 fp32 round trip (zero + write + read back + half write via copy_) and any per-call operand repack are extra implementation traffic that is counted in the measured time but is diagnostic, not part of Q. Both timed run() bodies pay the zero-fill, atomics and half-dtype round trip. On the Triton side the (N, K) transpose of B is paid only on the first call per tensor (cached, impl_triton.py 63-71, 264), which the decided rule forbids, so the Triton column is not comparable to contract-conforming implementations; the cuTile side has no repack and is comparable.
